hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext:
[agy-discipline plugin] Personal cost-discipline rules on top of antigravity-for-claude-code's own routing policy:

1. PRE-FLIGHT: Run `agy-doctor` once per session before the first delegation — it confirms auth/model availability in seconds, the cheapest place a dead tier shows up. It will NOT catch a quota exhausted only at call time.

2. SHORT LEASH: Don't let a single agy call, or any subagent/harness wrapping it, run past the plugin's configured `timeout` (antigravity-for-claude-code default: 5m) without a progress signal. A prior incident: a subagent's own ~10min outer wait, stacked on top of agy's internal retry/backoff, burned 52,533 Claude tokens discovering a 429 that a short leash would have surfaced in under a minute. Prefer `structured_output: on` so failures classify from structured JSON instead of looking like plain latency. On RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED/HTTP 429: do not retry, do not call agy again this session (the error reports a reset time) — fall back to doing the work directly and say so plainly.

3. SESSION COST-AWARENESS: Track whether delegation is paying off this session, not just per-task in isolation. A task that looks above break-even in isolation (e.g. sorting a column) can still be a net loss once round-trip spec+wait+verify is counted. If a delegation clearly cost more than doing it directly would have, say so plainly rather than letting it pass silently.

4. VERIFY, ALWAYS: Never trust agy's self-reported success — independently check the actual result (re-run the gate, spot-check values against source data) before treating it as final.

This plugin only injects discipline context; the routing policy itself (when to delegate) lives in antigravity-for-claude-code's `coding_policy`. Toggle this plugin's rules via its `enabled` userConfig.
